newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan firms win orders for China chemical plants.
newsitem.headline: Japan firms win orders for China chemical plants.

text.p: Major Japanese construction firms are rushing to build chemical plants in China to take advantage of the country's growing demand for synthetic fibre.

China's Petro-Chemical International Co placed two sets of orders on Wednesday with Japanese firms for the construction of plants to make purified terephthalic acid (PTA), a basic material used in polyester fibre.

Chiyoda Corp and Marubeni Corp received a $100 million order from the state-run Chinese company for a plant in the central province of Henan, while Mitsui Engineering & Shipbuilding Co Ltd and trading firms Itochu Corp and Mitsui & Co Ltd won an order for a similar amount from the company for a plant in the city of Tianjin, near the capital of Beijing.
"While demand for synthetic fibre is growing rapidly amid economic expansion, China is hoping to reduce its dependence on imports," a Mitsui Engineering spokesman said.
Chiyoda said the Henan plant is expected to be completed at the end of 1999 and will have an annual production capacity of 225,000 tonnes.
The Tianjin plant is expected to be completed in early 2000 and will have an annual production capacity of 250,000 tonnes, Mitsui Engineering said.
